2608.20331.title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
2608.20331.paper_summary: Personalized interpretation of medical reports has emerged as an increasingly important need among patients. Addressing this need requires both evidence-grounded medical factuality and context-dependent patient communication, yet existing medical vision-language tasks do not adequately capture these dual requirements. To bridge this gap, we introduce Patient-oriented Medical Report Interpretation (PMRI), a novel open-ended multimodal generation task that requires models to explain medical reports in accurate and accessible language based on a user's query and dialogue history. These two objectives differ fundamentally in their verifiability, yet remain tightly coupled, making them difficult to optimize jointly under conventional supervised fine-tuning and holistic reinforcement learning paradigms. To address this challenge, we propose G-CARL, a grounded, checklist-aligned reinforcement learning framework that combines multi-source retrieval for atomic claim verification with context-aware, instance-specific weighted checklists for response coverage, providing structured supervision for factuality, user-demand satisfaction, and expression quality without constraining response diversity. We further construct MMedReport, a real-world PMRI benchmark, along with a clinician-designed three-dimensional evaluation protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate that G-CARL consistently outperforms existing post-training baselines in overall quality, claim-level precision, and checklist recall. Pairwise preference evaluation by clinicians further confirms that G-CARL produces interpretations that are more accurate and better aligned with patient needs.
2608.20331.paper_summary_zh: 個性化的醫療報告解釋已成為患者日益重要的需求。滿足這一需求需要基於證據的醫療事實性和依賴於上下文的患者溝通，然而現有的醫療視覺-語言任務未能充分捕捉這兩個要求。為了填補這一空白，我們提出了以患者為導向的醫療報告解釋（PMRI），這是一項新穎的開放式多模態生成任務，要求模型根據用戶的查詢和對話歷史以準確且易於理解的語言解釋醫療報告。這兩個目標在可驗證性上根本不同，但仍然緊密相連，使得在傳統的監督微調和整體強化學習範式下難以共同優化。為了解決這一挑戰，我們提出了G-CARL，一個以基礎為依據、對照清單對齊的強化學習框架，結合了多源檢索以進行原子主張驗證，並使用上下文感知的實例特定加權清單來確保回應的覆蓋範圍，為事實性、用戶需求滿足和表達質量提供結構化的監督，而不限制回應的多樣性。我們進一步構建了MMedReport，一個現實世界的PMRI基準，以及一個由臨床醫生設計的三維評估協議。大量實驗表明，G-CARL在整體質量、主張級精確度和清單召回率方面始終優於現有的後訓練基準。臨床醫生的成對偏好評估進一步證實，G-CARL產生的解釋更準確，且更符合患者需求。
